elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Client may assign without approval only to a “financially responsible affiliate,” which is narrower than any affiliate.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: No approval is required for Client’s assignment to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all of its assets.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Vendor may assign to a financially responsible affiliate without Client’s approval.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Any required approval, including Client’s approval of Vendor assignments, may not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no prohibition on assignment to a Client competitor.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause grants Vendor no termination right arising from Client’s change of control.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: Only Client has a consent-free successor carve-out; Vendor successor assignments remain subject to prior written approval.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: Client’s successor assignment requires neither approval nor written notice, and Vendor’s requires approval rather than notice alone.
Non-successor assignments to financially responsible affiliates are exempt from approval for both parties.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Where prior written approval is required, it may not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.
